newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Tuesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose to 1.368 billion yuan from 1.139 billion on Monday with the 60-day contract still the most active.
Traders said the rates are likely to fall further in the next few days on prevailing expectations that the central bank will cut bank reserve ratios in the short term.
But they added the cut would not increase China's money supply greatly in 1997 because the central bank would concurrently set new limits on loan quotas.
Non-banking financial centres remained active and major state-run banks increased their trading volume, which indicated the market would be more and more active in the mid-term, traders said.
